title: Raised cup stitch
subtitle: Buttonhole stitches built over a triangle foundation to form a small raised ring
excerpt: Raised cup stitch is a three-dimensional stitch that builds a small padded cup or ring from the fabric surface. A triangle of foundation stitches is laid first, then close buttonhole stitches are worked in rounds over the foundation without entering the fabric, raising the cup away from the ground. It is used in stumpwork and raised embroidery for small flower calyxes, cups, and rings.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), raised stitch entries. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), raised embroidery chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Contemporary raised embroidery (stumpwork) practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Stitches laid on the fabric surface over which subsequent rows are worked without entering the fabric, forming the structure that raises the embroidery above the ground cloth.

content.text: Raised cup stitch begins with a small set of

worked in a triangle shape. Rounds of close buttonhole stitches are then worked over those foundations, with the needle sliding under the threads rather than piercing the fabric. Each round adds height. The result is a small raised cup or ring that stands clear of the fabric surface.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 strands, or fine perle 12; a stiffer thread holds the cup shape better

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Closely woven linen or cotton, held taut

items.label: Needle
items.value: Embroidery needle size 10 for foundation; tapestry needle size 26 (blunt) for the buttonhole rounds

content.text: Mark a small triangle on the fabric, about 5 to 8 mm across. Bring the thread up at point (A) at one corner of the triangle, carry it to point (B) at a second corner, and take it down. Bring it up at (B) again and carry it to point (C) at the third corner. Work two or three threads along each side until you have a triangle of parallel threads lying on the surface.

Bring the thread up close to one corner at (A). Using the blunt tapestry needle, work a close buttonhole stitch over one side of the triangle by sliding the needle under the foundation thread and looping the working thread under the needle tip before pulling through. Work stitches right along that side, keeping them even and packed tightly together.
Continue around all three sides of the triangle in the same way to complete the first round. At each corner, work one or two extra stitches to turn neatly.

For each subsequent round, work buttonhole stitches into the loops of the previous round rather than into the foundation threads. The needle slides under each loop in turn without entering the fabric. The sides of the cup rise with each round.
When the cup reaches the desired height, take the working thread down through the fabric at the top edge of the last round to secure it. Fasten off at the back.

attrs.heading: When raised cup stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The cup collapses flat after a few rounds
items.cause: The foundation triangle threads are too few or too slack.
items.fix: Work three or four parallel threads along each side of the triangle before beginning the buttonhole rounds. Pull the foundation threads firmly so they lie taut.

items.symptom: The buttonhole stitches bunch unevenly around the corners
items.cause: Too few stitches at each corner so the thread pulls tight rather than turning smoothly.
items.fix: Work two or three extra stitches into the same corner loop, fanning them out to spread the turn evenly.

items.symptom: The sides bulge outward rather than rising straight
items.cause: Tension is too loose on the working thread as each stitch is pulled through.
items.fix: Keep even, moderate tension on the working thread at every stitch. The loops should sit close together but not be dragged tight.
